title: Textbooks Are All You Need (phi-1)
hook: Train a 1.3B code model on a few billion tokens of 'textbook quality' data instead of raw web scale, and it scores 50.6% pass@1 on HumanEval — data quality standing in for size.
key_points: Introduces phi-1, a 1.3B-parameter code model, trained for 4 days on 8 A100 GPUs.
Data: ~6B tokens of 'textbook quality' filtered web data plus ~1B synthetic tokens from GPT-3.5.
Reaches 50.6% pass@1 on HumanEval and 55.5% on MBPP.
A 350M-parameter variant still reaches 45% on HumanEval.
Takeaway: data quality can substitute for raw scale.
content_html: Suriya Gunasekar, Yi Zhang, Jyoti Aneja, and colleagues introduced phi-1, a 1.3B-parameter code language model, to test a simple bet: that curating data quality could substitute for raw scale. Trained for just four days on eight A100 GPUs, phi-1 reaches 50.6% pass@1 on HumanEval and 55.5% on MBPP — strong results for its size and budget.
extra_html:
How it works

The training mix is small but deliberate: roughly 6B tokens of "textbook quality" filtered web data plus about 1B tokens synthetically generated by GPT-3.5. Rather than feeding the model the open web, the authors select for material that reads like a clean, well-structured lesson, on the theory that better examples teach more per token.

Why it matters

The headline is the swap of quality for quantity. A model trained on a few billion carefully chosen tokens competes with far larger, web-scale code models, and even a 350M-parameter variant still reaches 45% on HumanEval. The result helped popularize the small, high-quality-data recipe that the later phi models built on.

related.title: Phi-3: A Capable Language Model on Your Phone
related.hook: Microsoft's Phi-3 Mini matches much larger models on reasoning benchmarks by training on heavily filtered, 'textbook-quality' data - and is small enough to run on a phone.

related.title: Chinchilla: Compute-Optimal Scaling
related.hook: Most giant models were starved of data. Chinchilla showed that for a fixed compute budget you should grow parameters and tokens together — and a smaller, longer-trained model won.

related.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning LMs with Self-Generated Instructions
related.hook: Instead of paying humans to write instruction data, have the model write its own — bootstrap instructions, inputs, and outputs from its own generations, filter, and fine-tune.
